alerts.name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
alerts.desc: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was identified in the query parameter 'q'. User input is reflected in the HTTP response body without contextual encoding.
alerts.solution: Contextually encode all user-controlled data before rendering into the HTML DOM. Enforce a strong Content-Security-Policy.
alerts.otherinfo: The marker was reflected verbatim in an unquoted HTML attribute context.

alerts.alert: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.desc: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

alerts.name: Cookie without SameSite Attribute
alerts.desc: A cookie has been set without a SameSite attribute, which means that the cookie will be sent in cross-site requests, exposing the site to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF).
alerts.solution: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to 'lax' or 'strict' for all sensitive session cookies.

alerts.name: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header (X-Frame-Options)
alerts.desc: The response does not include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options to protect against Clickjacking attacks.
alerts.solution: Modern web applications should protect against Clickjacking by including X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN, or CSP frame-ancestors.
